subject: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for low-latency inference
messages:

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for low-latency inference

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have alignment on the Hosted vs Dedicated decision for FinPay's real-time fraud scoring use case.

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Peak QPS: ~1,200 requests/sec for token-level scoring (bursty around batch settlements).
- Latency SLO: p95 per-request latency <= 120ms end-to-end (inference + network).
- Model: custom-finetuned LLM ~2.7B with KV cache enabled and 512 token context on average.
- Data controls: no storage of PII in hosted logs, prefer dedicated isolation if possible.

Quick recommendation: Based on those numbers, Dedicated capacity is the safer path for predictable p95 latency and throughput. Hosted API can work for lower-throughput or non-SLAd use cases, but for sustained 1k+ QPS with tight p95 targets we recommend Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with the following configuration:
- Dedicated pod pool sized for consistent ~1,500 RPS with burst headroom.
- Autoscaling policy with scale-up threshold at 70% utilization and conservative cooldowns.
- Enable KV prefix caching and prefix routing for most frequent flows to reduce per-token compute.
- Use quantized model runtime profile (int8) we tested for the 2.7B variant — will save ~30% tokens cost while preserving quality.

What I attached: a short latency matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated (redwood-dedicated-vs-hosted-latency-matrix.pdf) and a proposed master agreement addendum for Dedicated capacity (proposed-maa-v1.docx).

Next steps I propose:
1) Run a 48-hour perf test on Dedicated with a synthetic workload (we can provision a small reserved pool and run overnight).
2) Share a perf-run report with p50/p95/p99 and cost projection.
3) If pass, sign the commitment for Dedicated minimal pool and schedule on-prem keys exchange if you want dedicated network isolation.

Can you confirm you want us to schedule the perf test this week? If yes, we’ll need a list of sample request payloads and a preferred maintenance window.

Thanks,
Dylan

Subject: Re: Decision follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated for low-latency inference

Alex — great questions. Short answers then a suggested plan: 

1) Baseline vs Burst sizing
- You can use a small baseline reserved pool sized for ~300–400 RPS and enable "burst capacity" (on-demand GPUs) for the 20-minute settlement window. That approach balances cost and predictability. If you want absolute predictability at p95 during burst, reserve to cover peak (higher cost). We typically see customers choose a hybrid: baseline reserved + capped burst with pre-warm policy.

2) Network vs inference latency breakdown
- From our benchmarks for a 2.7B quantized model on gpus we run: token-generation inference time contributes ~45–55ms median per request for the typical 512-token context path; p95 inference time depends heavily on batching and cache hit rate but we observed p95 inference ~70–95ms under steady load.
- Network (us-west region) and request routing adds ~20–30ms median; with edge routing you can shave a few ms but not eliminate network variability.
- Total realistic p95 you'd expect on Hosted is often >150–200ms at 1k QPS because multi-tenant noisy neighbors and auto-scaling tail sickness increase variance. Dedicated avoids noisy neighbor interference and lets us control batching windows and instance placement — that leads to much tighter p95 in our experience.

Suggested plan
- Do a 48-hour perf run on Dedicated but start with small baseline + burst so we can validate p95 during your settlement window without committing to peak-only reserve. We'll instrument tracing so we can show "inference vs network vs queueing" splits.
- We'll produce a cost model showing baseline + burst cost vs fully reserved.
- Contract note: minimum term for Dedicated varies by commitment (monthly vs annual). For the baseline+burst approach we can offer a 3-month minimum with monthly invoicing; for fully reserved peak pools we typically require a 12-month commit for the best pricing. I’ll loop my finance contact if you want exact numbers.

If that sounds good I can provision the test and send an invite for a 30-min kickoff to align payloads and window.

Thanks,
Dylan
